fact: The Korvane Employee Handbook version 4 carries the document reference HR-HB-04 and this extract is numbered EXTRACT-C.
Employee Handbook version 4 took effect on 1 February 2024 and is owned by People & Culture under Ines Baptista-Okafor.
The extract reproduces Handbook Sections 3, 4, 5, 6, 8 and 12 for depot notice boards and welcome packs.
Where the extract and the full Handbook differ the full Handbook prevails, and a signed individual contract prevails over the Handbook to the extent it is more favourable to the employee.
Service with an entity acquired by the Company counts towards annual-leave tenure, but unpaid leave exceeding 30 consecutive days does not count.
A full-time employee with 0 to 2 completed years of service receives 21 working days of annual leave per leave year.
A full-time employee with 3 to 5 completed years of service receives 24 working days of annual leave per leave year.
A full-time employee with 6 to 9 completed years of service receives 27 working days of annual leave per leave year.
A full-time employee with 10 or more completed years of service receives 30 working days of annual leave per leave year.
In the year of joining, annual leave is credited at one twelfth of the annual figure per full calendar month of employment, rounded up to the nearest half day.
The annual leave year at Korvane is the calendar year, and part-time staff are credited pro rata to contractual hours.
Leave requests are submitted on form PD-12 in the intranet People Desk.
Absences longer than 5 consecutive working days must be requested at least 10 working days ahead, while shorter absences need two working days' notice.
The line manager is expected to answer a leave request within 4 working days, and an unanswered request is escalated to the Depot Manager or Head of Department rather than deemed approved.

Between 10 November and 23 December no more than one in five members of an operational shift team at GDY-1 or RTM-3 may be on annual leave at the same time without the Depot Manager's written consent.
The peak-season leave restriction is applied informally at HAM-2 by custom rather than by rule.
values: by custom rather than by rule

fact: Up to 6 days of unused annual leave can be carried over and must be taken by 31 May of the following year.
Leave days above the carry-over limit are scheduled unilaterally by the Company, which notifies the employee by 30 November.
An employee's own wedding earns two days of special paid leave that are not deducted from annual leave.
values: two days for the employee's own wedding

fact: Bereavement leave is four days for the death of a spouse, child or parent and two days for a sibling or grandparent.
values: four days on the death of a spouse, child or parent
two days on the death of a sibling or grandparent

fact: One day of special leave per calendar year is granted for moving house, on production of a rental or purchase document.
values: one day per calendar year for moving house

fact: 15 May is Founders' Day, a half day on which work ends at 12:00 for employees not on a live reefer-yard shift, who get the half day back as time in lieu.
Handbook version 3 of 1 September 2021 granted only 20 days of annual leave in the entry tier.
Employees whose old contracts quote the v3 leave figure are entitled to the higher v4 figure from 1 February 2024.
A sick employee must notify the shift lead or line manager by telephone no later than one hour after the scheduled shift start.
Office staff without a fixed shift must call in sick by 09:30.
Notifying sickness by text message or through a colleague is not sufficient unless the shift lead has agreed it in advance.
An electronic medical certificate (e-ZLA) must be available to the Company within 3 working days of the first day of absence.
Employees may self-certify absences of up to 2 consecutive working days, with at most 4 days of self-certified absence accepted per calendar year.
Sick-pay steps are counted cumulatively over each twelve-month period starting from the first day of the first absence.
Sick pay at Step 1, days 1 to 3 of absence, is 100% of base pay.
Sick pay at Step 2, days 4 to 33 of absence, is 90% of base pay.
At Step 3, days 34 to 90, employees with at least 3 completed years of service get 88% of base pay and all others get statutory sickness benefit only.
From day 91 of absence onwards only statutory sickness benefit is paid.
A return-to-work conversation is held after a single absence of 10 or more consecutive working days or after the third separate absence within a rolling six months.
Return-to-work conversations are recorded on form PD-31 and are not a disciplinary meeting.
Remote working requires completion of a 3-month probation period, and operations staff on a shift roster are not eligible.
Dispatchers may work from home only when the Head of Operations has declared a contingency such as an official depot closure or a flood warning for the Gdynia yard.
Eligible employees may work remotely up to 2 days per week and never more than 8 days in a calendar month.
Under Handbook v4 the core office days at ul. Łużycka 14 were Tuesday and Wednesday.
Core working hours are 10:00 to 15:00 on every working day, in the office or remote.
The home-office allowance was PLN 60 gross per month for employees working remotely on at least 4 days per month on average.
A one-off equipment stipend of PLN 450 for a monitor or chair is available once every 36 months against receipt.
Working from abroad is allowed only in EU or EEA countries, for no more than 20 working days per calendar year.
Work from abroad needs written approval from the line manager and People & Culture at least 15 working days before the first day abroad.
Expense claims go on form EX-7 and must be submitted within 30 calendar days of the end of the trip.
Late expense claims need approval of the Finance Controller, and approved claims are paid with payroll on the 10th of the month following approval.
In Poland the expense ceilings are PLN 118 meals per day, PLN 430 hotel per night with breakfast and PLN 1.27 per km for a private car.
In Germany the expense ceilings are EUR 36 meals per day, EUR 128 hotel per night and EUR 0.34 per km for a private car.
In the Netherlands the expense ceilings are EUR 39 meals per day, EUR 146 hotel per night and EUR 0.36 per km for a private car.
In Sweden the expense ceilings are EUR 41 meals per day, EUR 152 hotel per night and EUR 0.33 per km for a private car.
Swedish meal expenses are paid in SEK at the ECB rate on the day of travel.
In Lithuania the expense ceilings are EUR 29 meals per day, EUR 97 hotel per night and EUR 0.27 per km for a private car.
The country limits are ceilings on receipted costs, not allowances.
A receipt is required for every single expense item above PLN 65 (EUR 15), and alcohol is never reimbursed.
Flights are booked in economy for journeys under 6 hours, and rail travel is second class.
Taxis are allowed between 22:00 and 05:00 or when the traveller carries luggage above 20 kg.
A trip estimated above EUR 500 needs prior approval of the Head of Department.

A disciplinary stage may be skipped only with the approval of People & Culture.
Disciplinary Stage 1 is a documented informal conversation that stays on the personnel file for 6 months.
Disciplinary Stage 2 is a written warning that stays on the personnel file for 12 months.
Disciplinary Stage 3 is a final written warning that stays on the personnel file for 18 months.
Disciplinary Stage 4 is termination of employment, with notice or without notice in the gross-misconduct cases of 8.4.
A disciplinary sanction may be imposed only within 10 working days after the line manager became aware of the conduct.
The employee gets a written invitation to the disciplinary meeting at least 3 working days beforehand and may bring a colleague or a trade-union representative.
The disciplinary decision is delivered in writing within 5 working days after the meeting.
An appeal goes to the Head of People & Culture within 7 calendar days of receiving the decision.
Appeals are heard by a panel of two including one person from the Legal department, are decided within 10 working days, and do not suspend the sanction.
Falsifying a temperature or door-open record is gross misconduct under code GM-1.
Reporting for a shift with a breath-alcohol reading above 0.10 per mille is gross misconduct under code GM-2.
Theft is gross misconduct under code GM-3 and unauthorised disclosure of customer data to a third party is GM-4.
Deliberately disabling a KC-Tag 4 or KC-Hub 200 alarm is gross misconduct under code GM-5, and violence or threats of violence are GM-6.
Pending an investigation an employee may be suspended on full pay for up to 15 working days.
